goal: Give the next state of a chunked blob upload to a kappa-distribution registry, so a client always knows whether to send, resume, retry or stop.

app.name: upload-session
app.title: Upload session
app.purpose: Give, as a UML state machine, the next state of a chunked upload session from its state, the event the registry received, and whether the assembled content hashes to the kappa-label the closing PUT names.
limits: It does not move bytes; it decides what a session becomes after each event.
The 416 recovery read (GET on the upload URL) does not change state and is not an event here.

fields.name: event
fields.means: an in-order PATCH, a PATCH at the wrong offset, the closing PUT, the session TTL passing, or a cancellation

fields.name: label
fields.means: whether the assembled content hashes to the expected kappa-label

meanings.open: a session exists and no chunk has been accepted
meanings.committed: the blob is stored under its kappa-label
meanings.rejected: 409: the assembled content did not match; partial data is discarded and the session pin released
meanings.abandoned: the session timed out or was cancelled; partial content is discarded and the pin released

rules.why: KAPPA_DISTRIBUTION_SPEC_v2.md 3.1: a stored blob is immutable
12.12: a rejected session's data is discarded; the client starts a new one
12.10: an abandoned session is gone; the client starts a new one
12.10: no chunk within the session TTL abandons the session
13.1 Level 1: upload cancellation discards the session
12.11: a PATCH at the wrong offset is 416 and changes nothing; the client recovers the range
12.11: a PATCH at the wrong offset is 416 and changes nothing; the client recovers the range
6.4 chunked upload: an in-order PATCH appends to the session
6.4: the closing PUT with a matching kappa-label commits the blob
12.12: a kappa-label mismatch on complete is rejected with 409

app.otherwiseWhy: a session that received nothing it acts on stays open

properties.why: content that does not match its label is never committed
an expired session always releases its pin

stakeholders.name: Cloud engineer
stakeholders.text: Moves images, VM disks and datasets between clouds and sites, and needs every upload to end committed, rejected or abandoned, never half-stored.

stakeholders.name: Registry operator
stakeholders.text: Runs the registry day to day and needs every abandoned or rejected upload to release its pin so storage is reclaimed.

concerns.name: No half-stored blobs
concerns.text: An upload either commits exactly the bytes its label names, or discards its partial data and releases its pin.

components.name: kappa-registry
components.text: The single-binary registry for OCI, Git, S3, Nix and AT Protocol over one content-addressed store.

components.name: Prism page
components.text: The published GitHub Pages site: it checks the holo seal, sends the request to the verified guest in the browser and shows the answer in the reader's view.

threats.name: Mismatched blob committed
threats.text: A client closes an upload whose bytes do not hash to the label, and corrupt content is stored under a trusted name.

control.name: Label match before commit
control.text: A mismatched upload is never committed, proved for every request.

threats.name: Leaked upload pins
threats.text: Sessions that never complete keep their pins and fill the store.

control.name: Timeout abandons
control.text: An expired session is always abandoned and its pin released, proved for every request.

quality.text: A PATCH at the wrong offset never ends a session.
quality.measureText: Requests with event gap from open or receiving answered committed, rejected or abandoned.
